source_user: Two serving systems claim different tokens/s. Design a reproducible comparison. Scenario variant 42: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: freeze model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, topology, prompt/generation distributions, concurrency, warmup, stopping rules, and telemetry; publish raw request traces.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: compare the same model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, topology, software/runtime versions, batching policy, scheduling limits, and request distribution. Define whether tokens/s means generated-only or end-to-end output tokens/s, and report prompt and output tokens separately. Claims are not evidence until the measurement window, units, workload, and correctness criteria are identical.

Hypothesis: after these controls, system A's higher throughput is caused by a specific mechanism such as better kernel efficiency, batching/scheduling, memory traffic, or communication overhead; pre-register the expected effect size and the load range in which it should appear. Falsify or qualify the hypothesis if the advantage disappears under matched conditions, fails to replicate across workload strata, or is not explained by synchronized component measurements.

Controlled experiment: freeze all stated software and hardware variables, warm each system to a pre-specified steady state, and use the same prompt-length/output-length/concurrency distribution, arrival process, stop criteria, and failure policy. Randomize system order and interleave paired trials; use enough repetitions for confidence intervals and report medians and tail latency. Measure end-to-end latency (ms), time to first token (ms), inter-token latency (ms), input/output tokens, completed tokens/s, requests/s, queueing, batch size, utilization, memory/communication/kernel time, errors, retries, quality/correctness, and energy or cost if relevant. Publish versioned configuration, raw request/response traces with sensitive content redacted, seeds, warmup/stopping rules, exclusions, and analysis code.

Confounders and safety: control thermal throttling, clock state, placement/NUMA, background load, cache state, admission limits, dynamic batching, request cancellations, retries, sampling randomness, and measurement overhead; do not compare unequal quality or silently drop failures. Verify output correctness and safety on a held-out workload. Use a shadow run or bounded canary before production, retain the current system as fallback, and roll back on predefined error, quality, latency-tail, saturation, or cost regressions. Treat observational counter differences as evidence, not proof of causality, and repeat on representative workloads before generalizing.

quality_dimensions.coverage: covers assumptions, falsifiable mechanism, controlled comparison, metrics, confounders, failure modes, measurement plan, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.technical_correctness: conservative; separates throughput definitions and measured evidence from causal claims
quality_dimensions.reproducibility: matched randomized paired trials with frozen variables and published traces
quality_dimensions.risk_awareness: includes correctness, privacy redaction, canary, fallback, and rollback gates

risks: tokens/s claims may use incompatible numerator or measurement windows
trace publication can expose sensitive prompts or outputs
short or unrepresentative workloads can reverse the ranking
telemetry and warmup choices can bias results
evidence_required: exact model/runtime/hardware/topology versions and configs
raw timestamped request and response traces with redaction policy
per-trial token counts, latency distributions, errors, retries, and synchronized component counters
replicated workload-stratified results with confidence intervals and correctness checks

Treat observational counter differences as evidence, not proof of causality, and repeat on representative workloads before generalizing.

quality_dimensions.coverage: covers assumptions, falsifiable mechanism, controlled comparison, metrics, confounders, failure modes, measurement plan, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.technical_correctness: conservative; separates throughput definitions and measured evidence from causal claims
quality_dimensions.reproducibility: matched randomized paired trials with frozen variables and published traces
quality_dimensions.risk_awareness: includes correctness, privacy redaction, canary, fallback, and rollback gates

risks: tokens/s claims may use incompatible numerator or measurement windows
trace publication can expose sensitive prompts or outputs
short or unrepresentative workloads can reverse the ranking
telemetry and warmup choices can bias results
evidence_required: exact model/runtime/hardware/topology versions and configs
raw timestamped request and response traces with redaction policy
per-trial token counts, latency distributions, errors, retries, and synchronized component counters
replicated workload-stratified results with confidence intervals and correctness checks
